messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: control-plane heartbeat missing for region pdx1 (control-plane-agg). 2/3 collectors timed out, marking region UNHEALTHY.
Anya K.: seeing the same on the dashboard, control-plane API 503s spiking. autoscaler health alerts too.
Matt P.: oncall pinged, rolling to engage failover. tagging @devops-oncall.
devops-oncall: I'm on it. gathering quick checklist: 1) provider status 2) control-plane logs 3) routing state 4) capacity for failover.
Sasha L.: provider console shows "Networking disruption" for pdx1 zone A/B, partially degraded. link: https://status.provider.example/pdx1 (reported 4m ago).
Anya K.: can we warm sfo1 GPU pools? dedicated capacity is near 85% for gpus, but we have preemptible headroom. Starting request to bump dedicated-reserve-sfo by 20%.
Matt P.: creating route override now: set smart-routing policy to prefer sfo1, failover delay 30s. command: `redwood route update --region-preference sfo1 --failover-delay 30s`
devops-oncall: applied route override. watching global traffic shift.
incident-bot: Traffic shift: 6% -> sfo1 now, latency for users in PDX rising ~120ms for some shards.
Sasha L.: control-plane pods in pdx1 show 'CrashLoopBackOff' on controller-manager and auth-gateway. grabbing logs.```
kubectl -n control-plane logs controller-manager-0
2026-03-18T12:07:21Z error: etcd dial timeout
2026-03-18T12:07:22Z fatal: unable to sync leader election
```
Anya K.: etcd connectivity to the control plane storage looks flaky; could be a network ACL or provider BGP flap. Anyone with cloud provider contact?
Matt P.: pinging provider support. raising severity. Support ticket #INC-4728. Summary: control-plane heartbeat missing, network flaps, affecting etcd.
cloud-status-bot: Provider status updated: "Investigating" -> "Network fabric: packet loss between pdx1 rack clusters". ETA unknown.
devops-oncall: we should enable read-only fallback for critical inference endpoints in other regions. Triggering canary fallback and notify product. `redwood config set --region-fallback read-only`
Sasha L.: started rolling read-only config to global edge. API keys still valid, writes will queue.
Anya K.: cost note: shifting to sfo1 and using preemptible GPUs will increase egress and provisioning costs by ~30% for the next 2 hours. cc @finance for heads up.
Matt P.: adding throttles on non-critical batch jobs to free up GPU slots: `kubectl scale deployment batch-worker --replicas=1 -n jobs`
devops-oncall: we'll maintain traffic steering for 30m, re-evaluate when provider gives an update. setting incident priority P1.
Anya K.: drafting status update for customers. Short message: "We're experiencing degraded service in pdx1 due to network disruptions. Traffic is being routed to healthy regions, and we are actively working with the provider to restore control-plane connectivity."
Matt P.: next steps: 1) provider updates 2) confirm etcd quorum or promote standby 3) monitor error rates + GA fallbacks. Assigning tasks: provider contact -> Matt, etcd analysis -> Sasha, customer comms -> Anya.
Sasha L.: etcd snapshot copied to s3 for safety: `aws s3 cp /var/lib/etcd/snapshot s3://redwood-incident-backups/pdx1-1799901234.snap`
incident-bot: Incident channel pinned, runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pdx1-outage.
devops-oncall: keeping this thread updated. escalate to eng-sre for kernel-level network checks if provider ETA > 30m.
Anya K.: noted. thanks all. will post customer update in 5m. :white_check_mark:
